title: Countable locally compact Hausdorff spaces are paracompact and normal
statement: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff topological space with a countable base. Then $X$ is $\sigma$-compact (a countable union of compact subsets), paracompact (every open cover admits a locally finite open refinement), and normal (any two disjoint closed subsets have disjoint open neighborhoods). Compact subsets are understood with their subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology].
